record.original_question: Let G be a finitely generated group with a fixed finite generating set S and the corresponding word metric LS(∗). An element g is said to be distorted in G if LS(g n)/n → 0 as n → ∞; this notion is independent of the choice of the generating set S. For any, not necessarily finitely generated, group H, an element g ∈ H is said to be distorted if there is a finitely generated subgroup G of H containing g in which g is distorted. Do there exist finitely generated left-orderable groups in which every nontrivial element is distorted? Note that it is straightforward to construct countable(not finitely generated) left-orderable groups with this property using HN N-extensions and applying results of V. V. Bludov and A. M. W. Glass.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finitely generated group $G$ with a fixed finite generating set $S$, let $L_S(\cdot)$ denote the corresponding word length on $G$. An element $g \in G$ is called distorted in $G$ if 
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{L_S(g^n)}{n} = 0.$$
This property does not depend on the choice of finite generating set $S$. For an arbitrary (not necessarily finitely generated) group $H$, an element $g \in H$ is called distorted in $H$ if there exists a finitely generated subgroup $G \le H$ with $g \in G$ such that $g$ is distorted in $G$.

A group $H$ is called left-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $H$ that is invariant under left multiplication: $a \le b \implies ca \le cb$ for all $a,b,c \in H$.

Question: Does there exist a finitely generated left-orderable group $H$ in which every nontrivial element is distorted?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in the current Kourovka Notebook list of open problems in group theory. A web search did not surface any published resolution; related recent work on finitely generated simple left-orderable groups (e.g., Hyde–Lodha and subsequent papers) addresses adjacent properties (uniform perfectness, quasimorphisms) but not the specific distortion question. The status appears to be open.
